newsitem.title: USA: NPC agrees to buy 52 Pizza Hut outlets.
newsitem.headline: NPC agrees to buy 52 Pizza Hut outlets.

text.p: NPC International Inc. said Tuesday it signed a letter of intent with Pizza Hut Inc. to acquire 52 Pizza Hut units and associated development areas in North Dakota, South Dakota and Minnesota for $33 million.
The 42 restaurants and 10 delivery carry-out units generated nearly $34.3 million in sales during the 52 weeks ended in January, it added.
The deal is expected to close in early June, and will be financed through an existing revolving line of credit, NPC said.
NPC, based in Pittsburg, Kan., is the world's largest Pizza Hut franchisee and operates 540 Pizza Hut restaurants and delivery kitchens in fourteen states.
NPC said the latest agreement follows its acquisitions of 126 units from Pizza Hut Inc., which is part of PepsiCo Inc., and 31 units from a Pizza Hut franchisee in North Carolina.

After the agreement was reached, the general area in which these stores are located was affected by recent severe weather, including flooding, NPC said. It said Pizza Hut Inc. agreed to repair any damage caused by weather and flooding prior to closing to NPC's satisfaction. If any store is not operational at closing, the purchase price will be reduced to account for the loss of operation, NPC said.
NPC said it is actively reviewing opportunities to acquire units from Pizza Hut and is actively seeking franchisee locations that are contiguous to its territories.

Including this deal, NPC will have acquired 228 Pizza Hut units during the last 24 months, for an increase of over 64 percent in the number of Pizza Hut units operated since its fiscal year ended March 28, 1995.

"While the units acquired in this transaction are not generally contiguous to our existing territories, the size of this acquisition and geographical concentration affords us adequate leverage of our field supervisory staff," Jim Schwartz, president of NPC said in a statement.
Closing of the deal is subject to negotiation of a definitive agreement and approval by the boards of both companies and regulators.

NPC also said it plans to complete the acquisition of four units around Champaign, Ill., from a franchisee on April 16. The four units produced sales of nearly $2.9 million during calendar 1996 and will be bought for $2.5 million.
Through Romacorp, Inc. a wholly-owned subsidiary, NPC also operates and franchises 180 Tony Roma's restaurants, the casual theme restaurant Famous For Ribs.
NCP's stock edged up 25 cents to $10 on Nasdaq at mid-morning.
